title: Giving Simple Answers
subtitle: How to give clear yes and no answers — and what to say when the answer is no
description: Learn to answer customer questions directly and confidently — 'Yes, we have it.', 'No, sorry.', 'Unfortunately not, but…' — without being vague or leaving the customer waiting.
dialogueSubtitle: Dana calls Riley with a list of yes/no questions before she decides to upgrade her plan

vocabulary.definition: Used to introduce disappointing or negative news in a polite way.
vocabulary.example: Unfortunately, phone support is not included in the Growth Plan.

vocabulary.definition: A different option that is available when what you want is not possible.
vocabulary.example: We don't have a single-user plan, but let me offer you an alternative.

vocabulary.definition: To have something as part of a plan, package, or offer.
vocabulary.example: Yes, live chat support is included in the Growth Plan.
That is correct — the annual rate works out at $124 a month.

vocabulary.definition: Used to agree completely or confirm something is 100% right.
vocabulary.example: Yes, exactly — you can upgrade from Starter to Growth at any time.

vocabulary.definition: To say you are sorry for something that is disappointing or inconvenient.
vocabulary.example: I apologise — that feature is not available on the Starter Plan.

vocabulary.definition: Included as a normal part of something, without needing to add or pay extra.
vocabulary.example: Data export is a standard feature on all plans — you don't need to request it.

vocabulary.definition: A polite or formal question asking for something specific.
vocabulary.example: That is a common request — most customers ask about this before they upgrade.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Confirm directly that a product, feature, or option is available.
phrasalVerbs.example: A mobile-friendly version? Yes, we have it — it works on any device.

phrasalVerbs.definition: A direct but polite way to say something is not possible or not available.
phrasalVerbs.example: A single-user plan? No, sorry — our plans start at five users.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Confirm that what the customer said is exactly right.
phrasalVerbs.example: The annual rate is $124 a month — that is correct.

phrasalVerbs.definition: A polite way to give a negative answer, softer than a plain 'no'.
phrasalVerbs.example: Phone support on the Growth Plan? Unfortunately not — that is only on Enterprise.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Confirm that something is part of the plan or offer.
phrasalVerbs.example: Live chat? Yes, that is included in the Growth Plan and above.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Introduce an alternative when you cannot give the customer what they asked for.
phrasalVerbs.example: We don't have a free plan, but let me offer you a 14-day free trial instead.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Hi Riley. I have a few quick questions before I decide to upgrade. Does the Growth Plan [[include:to have something as part of a plan, package, or offer]] live reporting?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes, we have it. The Growth Plan includes a full reporting dashboard — you can track deals, team performance, and customer activity all in one place.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Is live chat support included too?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes, that is [[correct:right; exactly as stated; accurate]] — live chat is [[standard:included as a normal part of something, without needing to add or pay extra]] on the Growth Plan. Email support is available on all plans.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: What about phone support? Is that included?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: I [[apologise:to say you are sorry for something that is disappointing or inconvenient]] — [[unfortunately:used to introduce disappointing or negative news in a polite way]] not on the Growth Plan. Phone support is only available on the Enterprise Plan. Let me offer you the live chat as an [[alternative:a different option that is available when what you want is not possible]] — most customers find it just as fast.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Understood. Can I export my data if I cancel?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes, [[exactly:used to agree completely or confirm something is 100% right]] — data export is a standard feature on all plans. It's yours, so you can take it with you any time.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Last [[request:a polite or formal question asking for something specific]] — do you have a plan for just two users? We're a small team.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: No, sorry — our plans start at five users. But let me offer you the Starter Plan at $49 a month. It covers up to five users, so you have room to grow and the price stays the same.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: That sounds fine actually. Can I upgrade to Growth later if I need to?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Yes, we have it — you can upgrade at any time with no fee. Your data moves with you automatically.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the customer's question, then decide which response (A, B, or C) is best. Discuss your reasoning, then click to check — and read why.

items.customerLine: Does the plan include unlimited storage?
options: I'm not sure — let me check the details and get back to you.
Unfortunately not — storage is limited to 100GB on the Growth Plan. But let me offer you the Enterprise Plan as an alternative — it includes unlimited storage.
Yes, I think so — most of our plans include a lot of storage.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives a direct no, explains the actual limit, and immediately offers an alternative. A delays the answer when you already know it. C is vague and inaccurate — never guess when you know the facts.

items.customerLine: Is live chat support included in the monthly price?
options: Yes, that is correct — live chat is included in the Growth Plan and above.
Yes, we have it — but I would have to check exactly which plans include it.
Support is included, but I am not sure in what form.
items.explanation: A is correct. It says yes clearly, confirms it with 'that is correct', and adds the key detail about which plans. B answers yes but sounds uncertain when you should know the answer. C is too vague to be useful.

items.customerLine: Can I cancel at any time?
options: I would have to check our cancellation policy before I can say for sure.
It depends on whether you pay monthly or annually.
Yes — monthly plans can be cancelled at any time. Annual plans run until the end of the billing year, so let me explain how that works.
items.explanation: C is correct. It leads with yes, then gives the honest full picture with the nuance about monthly vs annual. A sounds uncertain when you should know your own policy. B starts with the limitation instead of the yes — the customer hears a negative first.

items.customerLine: Do you have a plan for just one user?
options: Unfortunately not — our plans start at five users. But let me offer you the Starter Plan as the closest option — it is $49 a month and gives you room to grow at the same price.
No, sorry — we only do team plans.
I would have to look into that for you.
items.explanation: A is correct. It gives a direct no, explains the minimum, and immediately turns it into a helpful next step. B just says no without offering anything else — the conversation stops there. C delays when you could answer now.

profileMatch.instructions: Read the three customer situations. As a group, decide what type of answer each one will get — a clear yes, a clear no with an alternative, or a yes with conditions. Use phrases from this lesson to explain your choices. Click 'Check Matches' when you agree.

profiles.name: Tom asks: 'Is there a free trial?'
profiles.description: Tom is evaluating Brightline and asks directly whether a free trial exists. The answer is simple and positive — there is a 14-day trial available to all new customers, no payment needed.

profiles.name: Yuki asks: 'Do you have a single-user plan?'
profiles.description: Yuki works alone and wants the most basic option. Unfortunately, all Brightline plans start at five users. There is no single-user plan — but there is a good next step to offer.

profiles.name: Carlos asks: 'Can I cancel at any time?'
profiles.description: Carlos wants to know about cancellation before he commits. Monthly customers can cancel any time, but annual customers are billed for the full year. The answer is yes — but it depends.

options.label: Yes, we have it
options.description: A clear, direct yes. The answer is positive and straightforward — no conditions, no limitations to explain. Lead with yes and add the key detail.

options.label: No, sorry — but here is an alternative
options.description: A direct no, followed immediately by the best alternative. Don't just say no and stop — offer the next best option so the conversation keeps moving.

options.label: Yes, but…
options.description: The answer is yes, but there are conditions the customer needs to know. Lead with yes, then explain the nuance honestly so the customer isn't surprised later.

finishTheLine.instructions: The salesperson's line has been cut off. As a group, discuss how you would finish it. Try to use phrases from this lesson — like 'Yes, that is included', 'Unfortunately not', or 'Let me offer you…'. There is no single correct answer — compare your ideas, then click to see one possible answer.
